newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm early, aided by no Fed hike.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm early, aided by no Fed hike.

text.p: Singapore shares rose early on Thursday, underpinned by the return of institutional demand after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged.
Dealers said foreign funds were buying selectively but more buy orders for core stocks were seen helping to firm sentiment.

"Blue chips are partly benefitting from no hike in interest rates after the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committe) meeting," a remisier said. Positive Singapore April non-oil export figures of 5.9 percent on Tuesday also lent support, he added.
At 0130 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 9.81 points at 2,063.80 on a moderate volume of 48 million shares.
Singapore stocks were also playing catch-up with regional bourses after the U.S. rates news as the market was shut on Wednesday for a public holiday.
Retail buyers were seen in the Malaysian over-the-counter market, driven by bargain-hunting after recent falls.

HongKong Land led actives up US$0.03 at US$2.72, and Renong Berhad up Singapore $0.10 at S$1.95. Shipping-based Hai Sun Hup saw its warrants rise to a high of S$0.37 cents before retreating, with some takeover rumours seen fuelling activity.
Foreign tranches of DBS, OCBC, UOB banks and SIA lost ground mainly due to profit taking.
